artifacts.summary: Confirms .deploy-lock/ is missing from all three enumeration sites, finds three more mutex/lock artifacts (.scope-lock/, .commit-lock/, .errors.lock) with the same gap via the sweep, notes the historical tracked file is already untracked (via plain git rm, not --cached), and recommends a shared-lib single-source fix for the two check-runtime-file-tracking.sh lists plus updates to two test fixtures that mirror the gitignore block.

memory_candidates.content: This repo has a live single-source-of-truth precedent for keeping two lint/check scripts' pattern lists in agreement: scripts/lib/task-reference-patterns.sh is sourced by both check-task-references.sh (repo-wide lint) and hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh (write-time gate), so neither defines its detection regex locally. When a task needs two scripts to agree on an enumerated pattern set (e.g. check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's EPHEMERAL_PROBES vs b_patterns arrays), extracting a shared scripts/lib/*.sh array is the established idiom here, not a novel invention.

gitignore glob **/.lock/ only matches directories literally named .lock; sibling mutex directories with different names (.scope-lock/, .commit-lock/, .deploy-lock/) are invisible to that one line and need their own explicit patterns. When auditing a runtime-file ignore policy built around a directory-name mutex convention, grep the source scripts for every distinct mutex/lock directory NAME rather than assuming one glob pattern covers the whole family.
